title: Specific Knowledge: why it can't be trained and how to find yours
summary: Naval explains that getting paid at scale requires accountability, leverage and specific knowledge, and that specific knowledge is the hardest to grasp. It can't be taught in a class, is found by following genuine curiosity and innate talent, feels like play to you but looks like work to others, and is often spotted first by people who know you well.

principles.text: To make money you need accountability, leverage and specific knowledge: why you, at scale, and not someone else.
principles.quote: If you want to make money you have to get paid at scale. And why you, that’s accountability, at scale, that’s leverage, and just you getting paid as opposed to somebody else getting paid , that’s specific knowledge.

principles.text: Specific knowledge can't be trained, or else you become replaceable and paid the minimum.
principles.quote: If you can be trained for it, if you can go to a class and learn specific knowledge, then somebody else can be trained for it too, and then we can mass-produce and mass-train people.

principles.text: Find specific knowledge by following your innate talents and genuine curiosity, not the hottest field.
principles.quote: So, specific knowledge is found much more by pursuing your innate talents, your genuine curiosity, and your passion. It’s not by going to school for whatever is the hottest job, it’s not for going into whatever field investors say is the hottest.

principles.text: Be fully into your domain: with leverage and compounding, being slightly more right pays hundreds of times more.
principles.quote: if you’re operating with 1,000 times leverage and somebody is right 80% of the time, and somebody else is right 90% of time, the person who’s right 90% of the time will literally get paid hundreds of times more by the market

principles.text: Look back at your own life to see what you're actually good at; real specific knowledge feels like play.
principles.quote: it’s more found by observation. You almost have to look back on your own life and see what you’re actually good at.

principles.text: Schooling and training amplify specific knowledge you already have, but the part you get paid for is the specific knowledge itself.
principles.quote: you need your schooling, you need your training to be able to capitalize on the best specific knowledge, but the part of it that you’re going to get paid for is the specific knowledge.
